case_studies.title: Is GraphRAG Needed? From Basic RAG to Graph-/Agentic Solutions with Context Optimization
case_studies.abstract: As advanced RAG variants like GraphRAG and Agentic RAG emerge, one leading question is when and how to use them. Here, we introduce a framework for different RAG scenarios evaluation and comparison on semi-structured knowledge bases, including regular RAG, GraphRAG, Modular RAG and Agentic RAG. We provide implementation for 9 standardized RAG scenarios, and conduct experiments for a comprehensive comparison. These scenarios are designed for real use cases regarding data and domain restrictions, spanning from simple document-based retrieval to advanced features such as hybrid text-graph retriev
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of determining when to use advanced variants of Retrieval-Augmentation-Generation (RAG) models, by building a framework to evaluate and compare different RAG scenarios. The authors implemented 9 standardized RAG scenarios and conducted experiments to compare their performance. The result provides a comprehensive comparison of regular RAG, GraphRAG, Modular RAG, and Agentic RAG models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on natural language processing and information retrieval models, but may be relevant to IT teams involved in AI or machine learning development.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: Basic RAG vs more advanced RAG variants is a topic of interest in academic circles, but this study is somewhat generic. Relevance: While GraphRAG relates to graph-based knowledge retrieval, it's not an IT-centric or SaaS-specific paper. Value: The authors provide implementations for 9 RAG scenarios and perform experiments, which could be used to build or propose services for a client within 90 days.

case_studies.title: LCAi: Life Cycle Assessment with big data fusion and retrieval-augmented generation-assisted interpretation
case_studies.abstract: The interpretation phase of life cycle assessment often lacks structured mechanisms for translating quantified improvement opportunities addressing environmental hotspots into actionable strategic pathways under technological, social, and policy uncertainty. The result is a more structured approach to life cycle assessment interpretation. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI: From Foundations to Systems
case_studies.abstract: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI is a comprehensive practitioner's reference for building autonomous AI systems. The book covers the full stack from first principles to production deployment, organized around a central thesis: building great agentic systems requires understanding every layer of the pipeline, not just one. The author built a reference book that covers every layer of the pipeline for building great agentic systems. The result is a resource for practitioners to understand and build autonomous AI systems.

case_studies.title: RAVEN: Long-Horizon Reasoning & Navigation with a Visuo-Spatio-Temporal Memory
case_studies.abstract: Long-term robot deployment requires a compact and scalable memory that preserves fine-grained visual semantics, grounds observations in space and time, and enables efficient storage and retrieval. In this paper, we propose RAVEN, an agentic memory system for long-horizon robotic question answering and navigation. RAVEN stores visual embeddings with pose and time in a vector database, and grounds retrieval in a spatial map to answer queries and navigate to goals. By operating directly on visual embeddings, RAVEN avoids lossy image-to-text captioning and enables accurate semantic, spatial, and t
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of long-term robot navigation and question answering by building a memory system called RAVEN. RAVEN stores visual embeddings with pose and time in a vector database, allowing for efficient storage and retrieval. The result is a system that enables accurate semantic, spatial, and temporal understanding for robots.
